## 1. Minimum change and frozen boundary

Add two separately named ports and shared methods on the existing plain readers. Existing ReservationReadPort and LegacyTurnReadPort, public signatures/constructors, context records and singleton enums remain byte-identical. Existing old entry methods continue old semantics, including R1 SINGLE_READER_TEST/RC and R2 R2_INTERNAL_RR_TEST/f2eR2ReaderTransactionManager. No old entry silently accepts a shared token. New methods are MANDATORY/readOnly on the actual f2eReaderTransactionManager; no alias/default manager, nested owner or new transaction. Names: SharedReservationReadPortV1.readSharedByScope and SharedLegacyReadPortV1.readSharedForDate. Only exact-date R1 scope (desde=hasta=date) and same exact R2 salon/date are admissible; no new shared by-ID route.

No second reader/query implementation: refactor each existing reader/executor/mapper to a single internal acquisition/mapping path, preserving old callers and old results. New overloads supply distinct shared execution metadata. Mapping uses a private neutral evidence view populated either by the original context or by validated SharedReadEvidenceV1; it NEVER constructs an old SINGLE_READER_TEST or INTERNAL_RR_TEST context for shared execution. Existing SQL/catalog constants, ordering, binds, scalar conversions, row validation, cardinality, anomaly policy, atom IDs, 26 R2 observables, 46 R2 provenance keys, 32 R1 provenance keys, fallback/raw fields and whole-set rejection remain unchanged. No source reconstruction after a call to an old entry, duplicate query, output relabel or permissive ContextAuthority lambda.

The seven MODIFIED main paths are exactly the two readers, two executors, two mappers and ReadSnapshotIdentifiers. ReadSnapshotIdentifiers gains shared-only overloads; old domain bytes/preimages remain unchanged. Each executor gains a shared overload and internal capture hook around its actual named setters/execution/materialization; old constructors and methods retain their behavior. Source SQL and typed bind values are reused, not replaced. No R3/R4/R5/V2 main or old context/port/catalog/row/DTO file is writable in A.

The ten NEW main files under admission/ have bounded responsibilities:

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| SharedAdmissionV1 | Owner-private session/reservation and admission state; physical binding verification, sequential source slots and destruction. No transaction opener, acquisition orchestrator, bean or public factory. |
| SharedReadContextV1 | Opaque, identity-sensitive one-use token reserved by the private session; no public constructor, deserializer, copy/equality authority or resource getters. |
| SharedReadEvidenceV1 | Strict immutable scalar metadata and pure versioned identity formulas; data cannot mint admission. Contains no JDBC/JPA/Spring type or effect. |
| SharedAdmissionDescriptorV1 | Immutable trusted expected endpoint/principal/history/schema-slice descriptor values. Its public scalar values are not capabilities. |
| SharedAdmissionSqlV1 | Exact bounded SELECT support catalog and typed per-phase plans. No schema creation, data repair, locks or material-reader SQL duplication. |
| SharedAdmissionCaptureV1 | Actual named-call and JDBC prepare/positional-bind/execute/row-shape/row-count plus metadata/control observations, bound to the registered physical resource/generation. |
| SharedAdmissionCompletionV1 | Private transaction synchronization and post-interceptor positive-completion fence; scalar receipt issuance after completion/cleanup only. |
| SharedReadResultV1 | Private provisional scalar payload, accessible only after the whole externally owned unit is positively completed and sealed. No successful prefix. |
| SharedReservationReadPortV1 | New R1 shared-only signature returning SharedReadResultV1<List<ReservationSourceSnapshot>>. |
| SharedLegacyReadPortV1 | New R2 shared-only signature returning SharedReadResultV1<LegacyTurnReadSet>. |

This is admission compatibility infrastructure, not an R6 physical owner/facade/coordinator, validity reader, comparison pipeline, runtime configuration or trigger. No production file opens REQUIRES_NEW, chooses a run, invokes the two ports in sequence, or registers a bean. Test-only owner/configuration exercise the contract on real Spring/JPA/PostgreSQL; they are not reused by production.

## 2. Private ownership and physical admission

The future separately authorized owner, or the new test-only owner, starts the physical transaction outside this library. Package-private construction/reservation/completion methods in admission/ bind the exact owner target/proxy, registered JpaTransactionManager bean object and name, DataSource, EMF, transaction-bound EntityManagerHolder/EntityManager/Session, logical JDBC connection, native PgConnection object and fresh generation, current thread, boundary/run/attempt/invocation and exact capture object. Object identity, not equality or descriptive UUID strings, controls admission. The only future main issuer path reserved is admission/R6AcquisitionOwner.java; it MUST remain absent in A and is not NEW or authorized for creation. Exact production-inventory/caller guards prevent an unapproved class in this package from acquiring package-private access. Existing approved classes cannot expose a public capability factory. Tests may reach package-private seams only from their frozen test paths.

Validate actual active synchronized RR/readOnly transaction, exposed correct Spring proxy and advisor target, actual registered manager's EMF/DataSource, joined shared EntityManager/Session, manual flush/defaultReadOnly, same ConnectionHolder/JDBC/native generation and endpoint/database/schema/principal against trusted descriptor. Inspect the actual resource via the already bound Session; never DataSource.getConnection, DriverManager, new EntityManager, default manager or unwrap-to-another-resource. The DataSource capture wrapper only delegates Hibernate's normal owner connection acquisition, records its exact resource and generation and checks close/return; a participant never calls acquisition. No entity/session/connection/stream handle escapes.

A session privately reserves exact context instances and scopes. State is RESERVED→ADMITTED→CONSUMED, with one expected source slot at a time; all failures make the unit ABORTED. Admission requires exact token identity, expected participant contract, run/attempt/invocation/thread/owner/proxy/manager/boundary/resource/generation/capture/catalog/scope/typed binds and the actual executor resource. Foreign/equal-copy/replayed/stale/reentrant/nested/wrong-order/wrong-thread tokens, altered scope, wrong advisor and already-consumed reservations fail before material SQL. Caller data cannot supply trusted physical/schema/source/capture SUCCESS fields. Public scalar evidence may be constructed for pure offline validation but grants no SQL authority.

The common session protocol has bounded participant identifiers R1/R2/R3/R4 and a privately supplied expected slot sequence, to avoid later modification of A's production code. A implements only R1/R2 bindings. It neither supplies R3/R4 readers nor accepts their test/provenance claims as shared evidence. Future B may consume the immutable common protocol through its own separately approved ports and exact guard edges; this dependency is explicitly proposed here and in B's manifest, not authority to implement B in A. No public generic registry, issuer, free-form participant name, caller callback that asserts success or caller-controlled factory.

## 3. Observed capture, descriptors and completion

Capture starts before first SQL, covers the entire externally owned physical unit and remains open through interceptor return/transaction completion/resource cleanup. Exact planned phases, normalized SQL bytes/catalog IDs, multiplicity/order, actual named Java/Hibernate bind calls, every actual positional JDBC occurrence/setter/type/value, execution entered/completed/failed, row metadata/count and same connection/generation must agree. Collection expansions are explicit and ordered. Missing/extra/reordered statements or binds, hidden JDBC/lazy/fetch work, failed executions and metadata/control anomalies abort. A seen-SQL inspector alone is insufficient. JDBC wrappers delegate interfaces directly; no reflective provenance reconstruction or guard bypass, new dependency or copied historical testinfra implementation. New capture code must separately validate actual driver events; fake callback lists are negative tests, not proof.

SharedAdmissionSqlV1 owns only physical/descriptor SELECT support. Exact catalog preparation follows frozen SQL-SUPPORT.json, including typed schema/relation binds and ordered relation allowlist. Owner-initial support validates actual successful V47/50 Flyway history/checksums and exact required R1/R2 schema/privilege slices using the trusted expected descriptor, not caller fingerprints. Administrative fixture migration/schema inspection/checksum setup is a separate test control plane. A participant cannot invoke setup or mutate the descriptor. No migration is added/edited/executed by production code.

R1_SHARED segment adds its own initial isolation/readOnly/resource/snapshot probes, exactly one closed scope material query, then its own four final probes. R2_SHARED retains its own closed four initial probes, members query, assignments query iff usable parent IDs exist, four final probes; preserve existing SQL/order/assignment-selection rules and typed occurrence counts. Neither segment substitutes global probes for participant probes. Initial/final snapshots and bound resource metadata must be equal. Each private segment maps one-to-one to global observed events. Owner/global descriptor observations and transaction control are separately ordered; helper primitives do not implement R6's complete global catalog, schedule or validity stage. Future R6 handoff must bind these accepted segments exactly.

After source acquisition, validate capture and physical observations, derive immutable participant scalar evidence, map once, and retain the result privately. SharedReadResultV1 exposes no usable payload during the transaction or after body return alone. It releases copied scalars only against the matching positive completion state for the WHOLE expected unit. One source's successful return never makes it independently releasable if another source or later phase fails. Failure during mapping/capture or any later participant prevents all releases.

Completion installs trusted synchronization inside TX, retains in-TX observations, and checks committed status, no rollback-only/UNKNOWN, callback/capture/cleanup errors and no extra SQL. The outer test facade/future separately authorized facade waits for normal return THROUGH the actual transaction interceptor and actual resource cleanup before the package-private completion fence can issue the receipt. Early afterCommit or afterCompletion alone is insufficient; caught/swallowed callback failures remain recorded. No postcommit probe pretends to observe the old snapshot. On every path, discard payload on failure, remove registry/ThreadLocal state, destroy reservations, invalidate generation before pool reuse and preserve first exception with later errors attached. Completion proof is from the actual manager/capture, never caller success flags. A pure later failure remains the future owner/facade's whole-result abort obligation, not permission to release an R6 result here.

# A Correction.1 — determinate scalar, descriptor and admission contract

NORMATIVE_DESIGN_ONLY. This document and SCALAR-SCHEMAS.json/SQL-SUPPORT.json specify exact data/encodings, not implemented observations. Public scalar construction/hash calculation issues no capability. OFFLINE-VECTORS.json proves only reproducible documentary preimages. No runtime, physical snapshot, database, privilege, completion or no-write PASS is asserted.

## 1. Exact encoding and commitment graph

SCALAR-SCHEMAS.json is the closed ordered field/type inventory. The field arrays, not JSON object key iteration, define wire order. Its SEQ/E/HashRecord/Subrecord/LegacyTextHash rules are normative. All record keys are mandatory even when their value is OPTIONAL-ABSENT or NULLABLE-SQL_NULL. Missing/extra/duplicate keys, unknown schema/type/tag/enum, malformed UTF-8/surrogates/NUL, noncanonical scalar/overflow, invalid collection shape and out-of-schema values reject. No reflection or Object.toString encoding. New typed framing MUST NOT replace any old participant source/hash framing.

Maps copied from original DTOs become NameValue lists sorted by unsigned UTF-8 encoded key, with every original entry exactly once. Original emitted source/candidate/backing/record-ID list order and duplicate-sensitive SQL rows/events are preserved; no global sorting or deduplication. An optional declared derivation/argument is ABSENT; an actually NULL SQL cell or nullable backing column is SQL_NULL. Empty text, empty list, ABSENT and SQL_NULL have distinct bytes.

For a named top-level record K, its commitment is HashRecord(the exact domain assigned to K, K, its complete fields). Other typed subrecords/lists use Subrecord on their closed wrapper record, never an untyped arbitrary JSON hash. The source-schema legacy fingerprint below is deliberately a different preserved algorithm.

The dependency graph is acyclic:

1. Privately trusted expected definitions/authority and source migration-byte manifest exist before SQL. Their typed Subrecord commitment is an input to UnitPlanV1. Private object identity bindings are established on the actual resource before its first SELECT; scalar UUIDs describe those bindings but cannot establish them.
2. SegmentPlanV1 commitments P and UnitPlanV1's Subrecord commitment are frozen before the first SELECT. They contain expected data, not actual initial observations, observed E, result hashes or receipts.
3. Owner-initial actual metadata/physical observations determine the actual full source-schema fingerprint, InstalledDescriptorV1 commitment D and each RequiredSliceV1 commitment S. D contains complete group rows plus preexisting expected-definition digests, never S; S may therefore bind D without circularity.
4. InitialV1 commitment I binds the actual descriptor/slice, exact UnitPlan commitment, actual owner/resource and retained initial probe. ObservedSegmentV1 O binds P/I and complete actual statements/conditional resolution/final probe; it contains raw physical row values, never execution-derived mapped source identities or result/receipt hashes.
5. E uses the previously frozen outer LegacyTextHash sequence exactly: [F2E-SHARED-PARTICIPANT-EVIDENCE-V1, F2E-SHARED-ADMISSION-V1, participant, run, attempt, readerInvocation, sourceName, sourceSchemaFingerprint, boundaryIdentity, resourceGenerationIdentity, I, P, O]. New R1/R2 X/L then derive from E and original scope/context inputs as specified by the corrected A design. No receipt is an input.
6. After mapping/complete closed validation, ParticipantResultV1 R binds E/X/L, the exact full immutable scalar payload and item count. Original source/candidate fingerprints and closed read-set formulas are preserved; R is a supplemental integration commitment, never a replacement semantic hash.
7. Only actual positive full-unit physical completion can issue CompletionV1 C binding D, the ordered participant I/P/O/E/X/R entries, complete global SQL observations and actual control/completion/cleanup events. C is not inserted into an upstream record. No result hash/receipt enters O/E or its own preimage.

The original sourceSchema fingerprint is prefixed sha256:, while D/S/I/P/O/E/X/L/R/C are lower-case hex64. These meanings cannot be exchanged merely because each contains SHA256 output.

## 2. Trusted expected values, actual observations and source schema

TrustedExpectationsV1 is installed privately by competent fixture/preflight authority under the exact owner. It is not received in a user request, arbitrary callback, public factory or an observed-row success flag. Expected endpoint/database/schema/principal/provider/driver/transaction versions, actual all50 migration-byte bindings, independent Flyway-resolved checksums and complete required definitions are fixed before material-unit SQL. An external immutable scalar copy is data only. Future executable authority must bind the actual trusted configuration/fixture inputs and their SHA256 before running; no unexecuted host expectation or checksum is fabricated in this design.

migrationManifestDigest binds the exact current protected all50 file manifest bytes. Every MigrationExpectation repositoryPath/sourceBytesSha256 must match that manifest exactly, with no missing/foreign/additional migration. SQL checksum/version/description/type/script expectations must be independently resolved by the project's pinned Flyway/control-plane setup from those bytes, retained and bound before the material transaction, never copied from the same untrusted observed history as its own expectation. Observed history must have exactly50 successful SQL migration records, positive unique contiguous installed ranks, unique exact (version,script), and the same independently expected version/description/type/script/checksum records; no failed/baseline/repair/unexpected/pending record. The actual current head is V47/50, not a claim that version numbers are consecutive1–50. Pending validation is a separate competent Flyway setup proof; absence of an observed history row is not proof there are no pending migrations.

The ten SHARED_INSTALLED_SCHEMA_00..09 SELECTs and their exact columns/order are frozen in SQL-SUPPORT.json. They extract the existing installed-schema algorithm without importing/calling any test infrastructure in main. Complete actual JDBC getString rows, with SQL NULL distinguished from empty text, produce:

- prefix = SEQ(UTF8(F2E-INSTALLED-SCHEMA-FLYWAY-V1));
- for projection i=0..9, cellBytes=SEQ(UTF8(N),UTF8(empty)) for NULL, otherwise SEQ(UTF8(V),UTF8(exact observed getString)); rowBytes=SEQ(all cells in original projection order); retain duplicates and sort rowBytes unsigned-byte order; block_i=SEQ(ASCII(i), every sorted rowBytes);
- sourceSchemaFingerprint = sha256: + SHA256(prefix || block_0 || ... || block_9), exactly as the old scalar algorithm. No typed new E() wrapping, OIDs, clocks, installation timestamps, principal, driver/version field or required-slice hash is inserted.

This ACTUAL same-RR full installed fingerprint must equal the separately trusted full-schema expectation. Both shared R1 and R2 sourceFingerprint functions receive this value in their original schemaFingerprint position, and otherwise retain their original complete byte preimages. Same source/schema/row inputs therefore preserve old source fingerprints. A different actual installed schema or supplied execution provenance may truthfully change a value; no cross-attempt or old49-versus-new50 hash-equality promise is made.

InstalledDescriptorV1 is DISTINCT: it binds actual sourceSchemaFingerprint, all50 history, actual endpoint/principal/provider/driver versions and the complete required-group rows, together with the preexisting expected-authority/migration digests. Provider/endpoint metadata is observed only on the already bound resource through the fixed pure JDBC metadata accessors, retained/captured and matched to trusted expected values. No getTables/getColumns or unplanned JDBC query, extra connection, default manager, setting change or metadata-derived source-fingerprint guess.

The full actual scalar rows used for schema fingerprints/required groups must be complete to EOF with exact expected fields/counts, no filters/limits or hidden winners. A configured capacity limit causes whole-unit abort, never prefix hashing. Raw observed row/event order remains in O; schema-definition comparison canonicalizes complete definition rows by unsigned encoded row bytes with multiplicities retained. Required key duplicates (column number/name, constraint name, index name) reject. Each relation exists with a nonempty expected column set and exact definitions; an empty successful relation metadata result is not missing-as-success. No unexpected row/type/nullability/default/constraint-validation/key/index-ready/valid/unique or privilege is ignored.

## 3. Closed groups and pre-acquisition descriptor connection

The common schema groups are fixed, with relation names unsigned UTF-8 ordered within each group:

- R1: reserva.
- R2: turno_instructor, turno_instructor_asignacion, turno_instructor_usuario.
- R3: programacion_asignacion, programacion_bloque.
- R4: programacion_ajuste_fecha.

A implements material bindings ONLY for R1/R2. R3/R4 are exactly the human-authorized COMMON metadata/decision schema reservation. There is no B/R6 import, reader, data query, coordinator or public plan-extension factory in A. All ten A main files must remain immutable when B later consumes the accepted contract.

For declared expected participants, the owner-private plan selects exactly those groups, takes their relation union in unsigned UTF-8 order and observes columns/constraints/indexes/privileges for each relation under SQL-SUPPORT's exact String binds. It also executes the complete installed/history probes. Owner-final repeats that exact resolved order/binds and compares the complete definitions/history/physical observations. This common metadata union does not coalesce R1/R2 source probes or R3's nine/R4's seventeen historical participant events. The R1/R2 material SQL/binds remain closed and unchanged.

For a group, expectedDefinitionCommitment=Subrecord(GroupDefinitionV1(participant,policyVersion,COMPLETE expected relation evidence)); observedDefinitionCommitment uses the same record with COMPLETE actual relation evidence, canonically ordered as above. The independently trusted expected record is not derived from current observations. RequiredGroupV1's expectedDefinitionCommitment is only an external input, never a hash of a group that contains itself. RequiredSliceV1 S binds exact participant/policy, expected authority, D, actual full source schema, expected/observed definitions and exact required relation list. Valid A R1/R2 reservations require the two definition commitments equal and full privilege/shape/history/physical checks passed. SELECT privilege true and INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE/TRIGGER false on every required relation; the independently provisioned/validated dedicated role must additionally be non-elevated and unable to perform DDL or sequence/side-effect writes, proven by competent later role/no-write controls, never inferred from these six booleans alone.

The ONLY future main connector is the exact ABSENT admission/R6AcquisitionOwner.java. Under B's separately accepted design, it obtains the private runtime's actual immutable captured descriptor view, calls B's pure SharedSchemaCompatibilityV1 before ANY R3/R4 reservation, then binds the returned common SliceDecisionDataV1 through the A private required-slice binding. A defines that common data record but imports no B type and offers no public caller-selected validation callback. R3/R4 private reservation has no no-decision overload/fallback; it requires the exact privately registered decision binding for this owner/capture/resource-generation/source/policy and matching actual D/sourceSchema/expected+observed definitions/S. Public/equal copied scalar decision data alone cannot register or mint a token. The actual future owner implementation must be independently audited for the mandatory helper call and no alternate path; this design does not claim that absent future caller exists or ran.

B validates the precise V46/49-required nominal slice on actual V47/50 plus exact current R4 V47 group before returning decision data. It does not equate an old full49 fingerprint with a required-slice digest or weaken R4 checks. A's own current private R1/R2 reservations never execute B logic; no combined implementation lifecycle. B may modify only its exact approved A guard path to add exact consumption edges later, never A main.

All actual source tokens remain identity-sensitive, owner-private, one-use RESERVED→ADMITTED→CONSUMED. Scope/date/zone/catalog, actual proxy/target/manager/resources/generation/thread and capture bindings are independently rechecked at admission and each stage. Wrong descriptor/source/policy/decision/hash/foreign or stale binding fails before material SQL; no public constructor or data hash proves physical ownership. Equal-copy token, replay, wrong thread/phase/scope/binds/manager/native object, nested capture/reentry and extra acquisition fail closed.

## 4. Exact plan/observed event linkage

All counts/ordinals are nonnegative U64; execution/plan/source ordinals start1, strictly contiguous where applicable. StatementPlan rowLimit, SegmentPlan timeoutMillis/maxObservedEvents/maxTotalRows must be explicitly positive bounded values selected by private competent configuration before SQL, never missing/default/unbounded. The later executable handoff must freeze their exact operational values; the scalar contract hashes those values deterministically and does not invent product-level defaults here.

UnitPlan expectedParticipants is exact, unique, scheduled order; participantPlans matches it one-to-one. Source scopes use exact closed bytes and the same exact-date salon set for R1/R2. R3/R4 reserved scopes are global/date-only. No scalar map or set order changes original SQL ordering: R1 salons use the original unsigned order; R2 SQL salon IDs and usable parent IDs use Java UUID.compareTo signed natural order; R2 scope canonical bytes use its original unsigned order. Hash vectors explicitly distinguish them.

The potential statement plan assigns stable planOrdinal across owner-initial, each participant potential segment and owner-final, plus segmentPlanOrdinal. Actual included SQL assigns compact globalExecutionOrdinal and segmentExecutionOrdinal. Conditional omissions do not get an executed SQL ordinal. Never predeclare an actual fixed later execution ordinal that depends on as-yet unread R2 rows.

The ONLY conditional derivation is R2_USABLE_PARENT_IDS_SIGNED_UUID_V1, exactly the closed method: reject null row-list; filter null rows; take nonnull turnId; distinct; Java signed natural UUID order. This is an assignment-query bind derivation, not source output deduplication or winner selection. Source row validation/atom/anomaly behavior remains in the unchanged mapping logic. The predeclared rule references the preceding member-result planOrdinal. After complete actual member decode, resolve the expected parent list BEFORE assignment SQL. If empty, no assignments SELECT; record ConditionalResolution with included=false, dependency raw-row commitment, empty resolved binds/occurrences and the unexpanded positional-template SHA. Otherwise resolve all expected actual UUID values/positional expansions and query once. No arbitrary observed bind value may define its own expectation.

NamedBindPlan order is exact original setter order. SCALAR has exactly one literal value and no derivation; LIST has ordered literal elements; DERIVED_UUID_LIST has no literals and the fixed above rule/dependency. JdbcOccurrencePlan macro order represents each SQL parameter occurrence, including repetitions. SCALAR expands one position; LIST_ELEMENTS expands one position per resolved list element; concatenation assigns exact1..N positions. ExpandedStatement is frozen before that statement executes and its Subrecord hash binds the precommitted plan ordinal, exact resolved named values/expanded positions/allowed setter tuples, actual expanded positional SQL hash and dependency-row commitment. Same parameter at four positions is four occurrences; collection ordering is not normalized away.

The actual capture observes named setter ordinal/name/declared type/runtime type/value lists AND every positional JDBC setter call/position/name/element/runtime type/JDBC type argument/value in actual order. Only exact pinned allowed setter tuples from the private plan are admitted, with no extra rebinding, missing position or guessed type. Named-to-positional values must match resolved expectation and each other one-to-one. Query/result shape and original complete scalar conversion are verified against the plan and closed catalog. Each observed prepare/execute/result belongs to the same actual bound resource/generation/owner, not merely a matching hash/SQL label. Failed preparation/bind/execute/row materialization, unknown SQL/metadata work, hidden JDBC/lazy/fetch query, pagination/limit/lock/write/sequence/function or extra statement aborts; no successful O/E/result/receipt is issued from that failure path.

RawRows stores actual column metadata, complete pre-mapping scalar rows, rowCount equal to row-list length and reachedEndOfResults=true. Cell type matches the declared column; SQL_NULL only where permitted; ABSENT is forbidden for returned SQL columns. All original conversion/shape errors still fail closed. Snapshot probes validate canonical pg_current_snapshot text and exact equality within the RR unit; they do not assert serializability. Principal/backend origin is explicit: the new four-column shared resource probe observes both directly; original R2/R3 two-column resource probes retain their exact historical shape and bind principal/backend to the already observed unchanged owner resource. No claim of an unexecuted extra participant probe. Same-object/generation checks and denial of unplanned SET/role changes are required in addition to those retained observations.

## 5. Payload integrity and positive completion

ResultPayloadV1 describes all original immutable scalar DTO data. For R1 it copies every original ReservationSourceSnapshot field, including original additional observable map and ABSENT historical target, plus full provenance; for R2 every GenericSourceSnapshot field/full26/46 maps. R3/R4 reserved scalar codec shapes mirror the unchanged public candidate/backing record signatures, explicitly bound by path/hash; these are data schemas, not A implementation of those readers or product mappings. All source/candidate/backing lists retain their exact closed order/bijection. The private reader result binds the actual validated copied payload and typed commitment, not a caller-supplied selected hash/list. Counts equal the profile-defined full emitted item count, not a successful prefix. R2's original logicalReadSetFingerprint may be retained as the supplemental originalReadSetFingerprint; no old source/semantic hash is replaced by the new R.

Shared R1 provenance explicitly has transactionIsolation independently observed and checked EXACT repeatable read, transactionAccessMode independently observed and checked EXACT read only. The exact physical-to-provenance rule is: current_setting(transaction_isolation) must return repeatable read; current_setting(transaction_read_only) must return on and the bound JDBC connection must be readOnly=true; then the closed access-mode text is read only. It is not falsely claimed that the setting SELECT literally returns read only. Shared mapper emits those verified values and reader independently rebuilds/cross-checks all32 normalized keys, including those fields. R1 old RC branch/literals/goldens remain unchanged. Shared label alone is insufficient evidence of RR. R2 retains truthful RR/read-only values and its46 keys. No old context is manufactured to reuse an old evidence label.

CompletionV1 is a private issuer's record, not an input constructor granting success. Successful receipt requires: all expected participant private states consumed exactly once in order; each final probe and complete capture valid; no rollback-only; actual manager COMMITTED outcome; normal proxy/interceptor return; no afterCommit/afterCompletion/callback/cleanup exception including one swallowed by a framework; capture sealed without extra SQL and native resource cleanup completed; all registries/ThreadLocals cleared and capabilities destroyed. Body return or either callback alone is insufficient. Full-unit failure destroys every provisional result and prevents all releases. A later pure pipeline failure remains future R6's whole-final-result abort obligation; completion never grants an R6 success result here.

ControlEvent arguments describe actual trusted JDBC/manager lifecycle calls, not arbitrary statement exemption. Its phase and lastCompletedGlobalSqlOrdinal bind actual interleaving with the SQL sequence: OPENING controls occur before the first SELECT; ACTIVE never permits an isolation/read-only/autocommit change; COMPLETING occurs only after the last planned SELECT and body validation; CLEANUP follows actual completion; RELEASED follows destruction. BEGIN records actual transaction-bound setAutoCommit(false)/begin control plus subsequent in-TX RR/read-only probes, not an invented wire trace; configure events bind actual isolation/read-only arguments; actual commit enter/normal-return/callback status and cleanup are retained. Cleanup may restore original connection settings only after completed transaction, no active participant and no additional material SQL, before pool return; actual acquire arguments bind original autocommit/readOnly/isolation, restore arguments must equal those originals. Capture must observe error entry even when a framework/pool later swallows it; no observable clean proof means no receipt. Synchronization inventory is owner-private and checked against its exact trusted callbacks at natural stages and before completion; foreign/extra/missing/reordered callbacks abort. Unknown control, rollback/UNKNOWN/exception or unexpected transition aborts and yields no receipt. Control observations are distinct from SELECT sequence; SQL observation commitment never includes its own downstream receipt. No postcommit SQL probe can prove the previous snapshot.

Completion participants match UnitPlan expectedParticipants and actual I/P/O/E/X/R/counts exactly, not a selected subset. Owner initial/final ObservationSequence commitments and global SQL ObservationSequence commitment bind all complete ordered actual observations. Actual source/group descriptor observations, initial/final snapshot/resource bindings and registered private owner objects must agree. Hash equality alone, externally constructed scalar data, endpoint equality or a ThreadLocal UUID cannot authenticate a manager, native connection, generation or positive completion. No resource/entity/proxy/stream handle escapes in any public result.

## 6. Rejection and evidence boundary

Every failed requirement is whole-unit ABORTED, never semantic absence/partial output. Preserve original first failure/protected cause and attached cleanup failures; the C diagnostic P2 is not repaired or made public-safe here. Future R6 uses only its own already validated public IDs and does not echo V2 context. Offline byte vectors and static schema validation prove no physical joining, complete capture, completion, SELECT-only privilege or no-write property. All those physical controls and old-mode regressions remain REQUIRED/NOT_EXECUTED until a separately human-approved executable lifecycle.

## 7. Correction.2 closed completion-control arguments

CONTROL-ARGUMENT-SCHEMAS.json is normative for EVERY ControlEventV1 before its typed encoding or inclusion in CompletionV1. It closes all twelve existing kinds, exact ordered argument names/types/presence/cardinality, actual extraction, entry/normal-return pairing, correlation, private identity, phase/SQL-cursor/state order, restoration grammar and failure denial. SCALAR-SCHEMAS.json alone describes record shape; it is never permission to accept arbitrary NamedCell names or to skip the per-kind validator. Missing/extra/duplicate/reordered/aliased/ABSENT or incorrectly nullable/type/value arguments fail closed. Known and after-observation values follow the exact ENTERED/SUCCEEDED table; no new event kind or failure success flag is introduced.

The SQL channel seals after actual normal interceptor return/cleanup; the private control journal remains append-only only through successful capability destruction, then freezes into C. This specifies the existing positive-completion record, does not add a public issuer or relax any actual failure/cleanup requirement. Unit-wide correlation comes from the actual parent run/attempt/unit/OwnerBinding and expected participant list; no redundant caller-selected participant context is allowed.

R1 provenance A-D1-01 remains CLOSED at design level and its accepted Correction.1 bytes/values/keysets are unchanged. No SQL, source formula, old entry, path reservation, trust source, runtime capability or cross-prerequisite relationship is changed by this residual argument-schema correction. The new nonempty documentary control/completion vectors are encoding/validation examples, not successful physical admissions.
